newsitem.title: GERMANY: INTERVIEW-Gehe boosted by pound gains.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Gehe boosted by pound gains.

text.p: German drugs wholesaler Gehe AG said on Wednesday it had gained some 400 million marks in "hidden reserves" as a result of the pound's advance against the deutschemark.

Gehe chief financial officer Karl Eick told Reuters in a telephone interview that the company would have to pay significantly higher sums in marks today for its most recent British acquisition Lloyds Chemists Plc, which it acquired in January, and for its AAH British operation, which it bought in May 1995.
"That translates into a significant level of hidden reserves for us," Eick said.
He said the reserve boost in the case of Lloyds Chemists was about 180 million marks. For AAH, the addition to reserves was some 250 million marks.

Gehe clinched the deal for Lloyds Chemists after a year-long takeover battle with Unichem, outgunning its British rival with a cash bid of 685 million pounds and securing itself a strong role in British retail pharmacy.
The German group acquired AAH, also a drugs wholesaler, in a deal which valued the group at around 400 million pounds.
Gehe said earlier it had made 230 million pounds this year by selling off non-core operations at Lloyds Chemists, in line with the takeover conditions set by the British government.
That had reduced the buy price of the British group by about one third, it noted in a statement.

Gehe reported a 15.4 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 226.5 million marks for the first six months of the year on sales of 12.4 billion marks, with Lloyds making a significant contribution to earnings.
Full-year profits would show an increase of 15 to 20 percent, Gehe predicted.
Gehe also said Lloyds had already been "smoothly" integrated with AAH.
AAH's 322 pharmacies have linked up with Lloyds' 904 outlets to create a new British retail pharmacy division.
